thread:
Maria: quick heads-up — noticed a p95 token-latency spike on /api/generate (route group=search-heavy) at ~02:03 UTC, looks like KV prefix hit_rate dropped sharply
Kevin: saw that too, dashboards show `kv_prefix_hit_rate` fell from ~92% -> ~61% over 90s window :eyes:
Olivia: any recent kernel-selection changes or batching heuristic rollouts?
Maria: we rolled the kernel selector tweak yesterday (adaptive-stride prefetch enabled) + default batching window bumped from 20ms -> 40ms for medium batch sizes
Ryan: interesting — increased batching window could change seq-length distribution and memory pressure, causing more evictions. What do cache metrics say?
Maria: here's the quick PromQL we ran in grafana: `sum by(route) (rate(kv_prefetch_evictions_total[1m]))` then `sum by(route) (kv_prefix_hit_rate{route=~"search-.*"})`
Olivia: flamegraph from the CPU profile (sampled during spike) points to kernel_selector::select_kernels -> kv_cache::evict_loop hot path
Kevin: perf-bot posted a summary: `perf-bot: spike-correlation report: 02:02:50-02:04:10 UTC: token_p95 +120ms, kv_cache_evictions +420/s, kv_mem_used +6GB (shard 12)`
Maria: exact log excerpt: ```
[02:03:05] WARN kv_cache: evicting prefix shard=12 mem_before=42.1GB mem_after=36.0GB evict_count=184
[02:03:06] INFO kernel_selector: fallback_to_quantized variant="int8" reason="batch_memory_pressure"
```
Ryan: fallback to quantized kernels is expected under memory pressure; quant kernels have different latency profile per token, could explain added tail
Olivia: do we have per-route reuse stats? I ran `sum by(route) (rate(kv_prefix_reuse_total[5m]))` — search-heavy routes reuse dropped ~3x compared to baseline
Kevin: dashboard panel suggestions: add token-level latency breakdown stacked by kernel_variant (fp16|int8|fallback) and overlay kv_prefix_hit_rate so SRE can triage faster
Maria: agree. Also add a memory footprint heatmap per shard over time + eviction_rate annotated with kernel selection events
Olivia: for quick mitigation — rolling back adaptive-stride prefetch on one canary pool reduced evictions and p95 started moving back down within 90s
Ryan: action items I can take: 1) add new grafana panels (kernel_variant token latency, shard memory heatmap) 2) instrument kernel_selector events as traces (trace id -> decision) 3) temp rollback on canary pool if metrics don't stabilize
Maria: thanks. i'll open an RFC with exact panel queries and wire up alert thresholds (kv_prefix_hit_rate < 70% AND evictions > 200/s)
Kevin: small note — add per-route sample set in logs so we can replay prefix patterns that missed cache (helpful for Optimize suggestions)
Olivia: re: profiling, attaching the perf link: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/abc123 — top stack shows evict + memcpy heavy paths, kernel selection overhead ~7ms median during spike
perf-bot: automated correlation: `kv_prefix_hit_rate` drop preceded token_p95 by ~18s, eviction burst correlated with increased batching_window. Suggested tag: `batching.window=40ms` for incident timeline
Maria: if no objections i'll flip the prefetch flag back on canary tonight and push the dashboard changes tomorrow morning
Kevin: +1
Olivia: +1, and i'll prepare a small replay set for Optimize team to run quantized vs fp16 comparison
Ryan: creating dashboard PR now and slacking link when ready
Maria: cool — will update incident thread once canary rollback is confirmed. TL;DR: kernel selector + larger batching window amplified memory pressure -> kv evictions -> lower reuse -> token p95 regression. Dashboards + traces should make this triageable next time. :white_check_mark:
